title: write-before-ioctl pattern for KEY_IMPORT avoids stack blowout
description: KEY_IMPORT takes key bytes via write() before the ioctl, not inline in the ioctl struct. The ioctl struct carries only metadata (algo, key_type, keylen, exportable — 100 bytes). This avoids embedding up to KEY_IMPORT_MAXLEN (8192 bytes) in the struct, which would land on the kernel stack on every KEY_IMPORT call including tiny EC key imports — violating the ~1 KB kernel stack frame guideline. The heap allocation via inbuf_append is exactly sized to the actual key. A reviewer might suggest 'simplify by embedding the key bytes in the ioctl struct' — do not do this. ML-DSA-87 private keys are 4896 bytes; future PQ schemes will be larger. The write-before-ioctl pattern scales correctly.
close_reason: Acknowledged: already implemented correctly, no code change required
